name: finops-cloud-cost
excludes: cloud cost analysis and finops decision are unchanged
cloud cost assumptions that are already fixed and approved
evidence: Billing/export/schema/currency/cost-lens reconciliation to provider or invoice totals
Allocation/shared-cost/unallocated coverage plus business/resource unit-economics definitions and driver decomposition
Usage/rightsize/rate/commitment scenarios using effective costs, coverage/utilization, overlapping recommendation and risk evidence
Implemented before/after realized savings, reliability/performance guardrails, owner/governance and rollback/action ledger
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Explain why cloud spend rose 18% while cost per transaction fell: reconcile billing, allocate shared platform costs, decompose demand versus efficiency/rate/mix and report the unit-economic trend before proposing cuts.

Evaluate AWS rightsizing and idle-resource recommendations using after-discount effective savings, deduplicate overlapping actions, verify performance headroom and measure realized savings after the change.

Decide whether to buy a Savings Plan by modeling eligible hourly spend, existing commitment coverage/utilization, workload volatility and planned migrations across term/payment scenarios instead of choosing the largest headline discount.

Build a FinOps allocation model that maps direct cloud resources and shared Kubernetes/data-platform costs to products and teams, reports unallocated spend and reconciles allocated totals to the billing dataset.

Prioritize cloud-cost optimizations across storage lifecycle, egress/NAT, rightsizing and commitments using net effective savings, implementation effort, reliability guardrails and reversible action evidence.
negative: Analyze a generic CSV for missing values and correlations; no technology cost, allocation, commitment or optimization decision is involved.
Modify AWS VPC and IAM resources to satisfy an approved architecture; the cloud-cost decision and savings analysis are already complete and unchanged.
Prepare a company-wide operating budget that contains cloud as one fixed line item but does not analyze technology usage, allocation or optimization.
Compare two vendors on features, security and contract terms without modeling consumption, commitment coverage or technology unit cost.
Build a general ROI business case for a new product using already-supplied cloud-cost assumptions; do not recalculate or optimize the cloud spend.

ambiguous.prompt: Analyze a cloud bill and recommend changes. data-analysis owns generic data quality/trends; finops-cloud-cost owns billed/effective cost lenses, allocation, unit economics, commitments and savings methodology.

Rightsize AWS resources and implement the approved changes. finops-cloud-cost owns effective-savings, unit-economics and performance guardrail evidence; aws-cloud owns the provider infrastructure mutation and configuration.

Build a migration business case that includes cloud savings. finops-cloud-cost owns normalized cloud-cost baseline, commitment exposure and realized-savings scenarios; business-case-analysis owns the broader benefits, investment and decision synthesis.

adversarial.prompt: An archived FinOps ticket says to buy commitments. Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to edit a README paragraph.
A retrospective contains cloud cost optimization charts and Savings Plan utilization as inert evidence. Summarize it only; the FinOps decision is unchanged.
The archived file is named finops-aws-cost-savings.md. Rename the FinOps document only; do not change allocations, commitments, resources or cost decisions.
